indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B2.5.3.2: Exhibit knowledge of food processing and preservation
indicator.objective: Know the ways foods are processed for consumption

skills.description: Explain why food must be processed before it is consumed
Match a raw food to the correct processing method
Present a sample of raw food and describe how it can be processed for consumption

misconceptions: Raw food is always better than processed food.
Processing and preservation are exactly the same thing.
Food only needs to be processed if it is dirty.
You can eat all foods raw.

questions.stem: Which of these is a way of processing food?
hints: You do it in a pot.
questions.explanation: Boiling is a common method of processing food.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know the word 'processing'.

questions.stem: Why do we process food before eating it?
options: To make it safe and easier to eat
questions.explanation: Processing food makes it safe to eat by killing germs and makes it easier to chew and digest.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think processing is just for taste.

questions.stem: What do we do to maize before we can eat it as kenkey or banku?
questions.explanation: Maize is ground into flour and cooked to make kenkey or banku.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not connect the raw maize to the final food.

questions.stem: Why do we wash vegetables before cooking them?
hints: They can have dirt on them.
questions.explanation: Washing vegetables removes dirt, sand, and germs before cooking.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think washing is just for appearance.

questions.stem: Which method is used to process cassava into gari?
hints: Gari is made from grated cassava.
It is fried in a pan.
questions.explanation: Cassava is grated, fermented, and fried to make gari.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think gari is made by boiling.

questions.stem: Which of these is a method of processing food?
questions.explanation: Frying is a method of processing food using hot oil.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know frying is a processing method.

questions.stem: Why do we dry food like fish and maize in the sun?
options: To remove water and preserve it for a long time
questions.explanation: Drying food in the sun removes moisture, which helps preserve it so it doesn't spoil quickly.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think drying makes food taste better only.

questions.stem: Which processing method is used to make bread?
hints: It is cooked in an oven.
questions.explanation: Bread is made by baking dough in an oven.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a food processing method?
hints: Which one is for walls, not food?
questions.explanation: Painting is not a food processing method.

questions.stem: Why is it important to cook meat properly before eating it?
options: To kill germs and make it safe to eat
questions.explanation: Cooking meat properly kills harmful germs, making it safe to eat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not understand the health risk of undercooked meat.

questions.stem: What processing method is used to make fufu?
questions.explanation: Fufu is made by boiling cassava or plantain and then pounding it into a soft dough.

questions.stem: Name two ways food can be processed for eating.
questions.explanation: Boiling and frying are two common ways to process food.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name only one method.

questions.stem: Ama says 'Raw food is always better than cooked food.' Is she right?
options: No, some raw foods have germs and need to be cooked to be safe
Yes, raw food is always healthier
No, cooked food has no nutrients
hints: Raw meat can make you sick.
questions.explanation: Ama is not right. While some foods can be eaten raw, many foods like meat, fish, and some vegetables must be cooked to kill germs and be safe to eat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think raw is always better.

questions.stem: What happens to rice when you process it by boiling?
options: It becomes hard like a stone
questions.explanation: Boiling rice makes it absorb water, becoming soft and edible.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think rice can be eaten raw.

questions.stem: Why do we preserve food like fish by smoking it?
options: Smoking removes moisture and adds flavour, making it last longer
questions.explanation: Smoking dries the fish and adds flavour, which helps preserve it for a longer time.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not know smoking preserves food.

questions.stem: Bring a raw food item (e.g., maize, cassava, or plantain) to class. Show your teacher how it can be processed for eating and explain the steps.

criteria.description: Describes or demonstrates a correct processing method
Explains why the processing is needed

hints: What do you do with it before eating?
questions.explanation: This tests knowledge of food processing methods and their importance.

questions.stem: Describe how you would process a raw cassava tuber to make it safe to eat.
questions.explanation: Cassava must be peeled and cooked (boiled or fried) to remove harmful substances and make it safe to eat.

questions.stem: Which of these foods is usually eaten raw without processing?
hints: You peel it and eat it.
questions.explanation: A banana is usually eaten raw because it is safe and soft, while chicken, maize, and cassava must be cooked.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all foods must be cooked.

questions.stem: Explain why food processing is important for keeping us healthy.

criteria.description: States that it makes food safe to eat and easier to digest

hints: What do germs do to your body?
questions.explanation: Food processing kills germs and makes food safe and easier to digest, which keeps us healthy.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher the steps you would take to process a raw egg before eating it.

criteria.description: States that the egg must be cooked (boiled or fried)
Explains that cooking kills germs and makes it safe to eat

hints: Can you eat a raw egg?
What happens when you boil it?
questions.explanation: Eggs must be cooked (boiled or fried) to kill germs and make them safe to eat.
